tasks.short: Sort chips and offcuts by metal, separate coolant and rags, record bin weights, report full bins and check bins before pickup.

steps.what: Machinist sorts chips and offcuts by metal type into bins for reuse or recycling
Machinist separates used coolant and oily rags for disposal
Machinist records bin changes and weights: written on the waste sheet today; after the change the container scale logs the weight and the machinist scans the bin label when emptying
Machinist checks a container flagged as full for wrong materials, and that the waste stream and weight on the pickup request match it
Machinist releases the pickup request for the checked container: by telling the shift lead today, by one release to the logistics coordinator after the change

tasks.design: A scale under each waste container logs the weight per metal and waste stream to the waste record in the {ERP}; the machinist only scans the bin label when emptying a bin into it. When a container passes its fill weight, the system flags it; the machinist checks the container for wrong materials and releases the pickup request once to the logistics coordinator. Sorting, separating hazardous waste and checking bins stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Weights were written on a sheet and full bins reported by word of mouth.
tasks.enabler_now: Container scales log weights per stream and send fill alerts.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed scrap loses value; sorting depends on care at the machine.
tasks.human_edge: Telling brass from bronze chips by look and feel.

reach.learn: Whether weight alerts cut emergency pickups.

evidence.claim: Container scales can log weights per waste stream and send fill alerts.
Companies must keep records of the waste streams they hand to collectors.

assumptions: Boundary: from scrap at the machine to bins cleared for pickup; transport and sale of scrap are outside.
Input contract: waste streams and fill weights set by the facility manager; fallback is the waste sheet.
Sorting, separating and the bin check keep their full time. s3 keeps 25 for scanning the bin label and looking at odd weights; s4 keeps 20 for the release, which replaces finding the shift lead.
Coordinator time is outside the machinist's savings.
research_questions: Does scrap revenue rise with cleaner streams?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep beyond the steps: scanning the bin label is part of s3.

approvals.approved_version: The pickup request with container, waste stream and logged weight exactly as checked by the machinist in s5, released once to the logistics coordinator's pickup list in {ERP}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: scales are fitted to only half of the containers, so half of the weights are still written and full bins reported by word of mouth (8.0); high: every container has a scale (15.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch coolant on the work piece, measure concentration, log readings, top up and adjust nozzles.

steps.what: Machinist checks that work pieces are properly lubricated or cooled during cutting
Machinist measures coolant concentration with a refractometer

Machinist logs concentration readings: written on the machine sheet today; after the change the digital refractometer sends each reading and the machinist selects the machine and checks the reading landed on it
Machinist tops up coolant and adjusts the nozzles

tasks.design: A digital refractometer sends each reading with machine number and time to the maintenance log in the shop-floor system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), replacing the machine sheet. Watching the cut, measuring, topping up and adjusting stay with the machinist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written on paper sheets at each machine.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital refractometers send readings to tablets and shop-floor systems.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a cut is cooled well enough is judged by eye, sound and chips.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a tool start to rub when the coolant misses the cut.

reach.learn: Whether logged readings show tanks that drift.

evidence.claim: Digital refractometers send readings to tablets and shop-floor systems.
Metalworking fluids are a health hazard; employers must control exposure.

assumptions: Boundary: from the running job to corrected coolant; tank changes are outside.
Input contract: concentration limits set by the maintenance technician; fallback is the machine sheet.
Watching, measuring and correcting keep their full time; s3 keeps 20 for selecting the machine on the device and checking the reading landed on it.
Readings are about machines, not used to rate operators.
research_questions: Do tool failures from poor cooling fall?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep beyond the steps: selecting the machine on the device is part of s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the machines get a digital refractometer at first, so half of the readings are still written (4.0); high: every machine has one (8.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read drawings and plan, look up cutting data, program and machine, assemble, measure, record results and test with the engineer.

steps.what: Machinist reads drawings and plans the machining steps for metalworking projects
Machinist looks up feeds and speeds: in tool catalogues today; after the change they come with the tool choice from the library, and catalogues are used only for tools not in it
Machinist programs the machine and makes the parts
Machinist assembles and fits the parts
Machinist measures the parts for inspection

Machinist records measured values: written on the inspection sheet today; after the change digital calipers and gauges send them and the machinist checks each value sits on the right feature and writes the few taken with plain gauges
Machinist tests the assembly with the engineer

tasks.design: The CAM system's tool library ({OTHER}) holds cutting data per tool and material from the tool makers' data, so feeds and speeds come with the tool choice. Digital calipers and gauges send values into the inspection record in the shop-floor system ({OPS_SYSTEM}). Planning, machining, assembly, measuring and testing stay with the machinist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cutting data came from catalogues and measured values were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: CAM tool libraries hold cutting data, and digital gauges send values to records.
tasks.still_hard: Catalogue data are a start; the machinist tunes them to the machine and part.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing an order of operations that keeps a thin part from warping.

reach.learn: Whether gauge data shorten first-part checks.

evidence.claim: CAM systems and tool makers' cutting-data tools give feeds and speeds.
Machine and gauge data tied to an operator login need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from drawings to the tested assembly; design changes are outside.
Input contract: drawings from the engineering department; cutting data from tool makers loaded by the tooling coordinator; fallback is catalogues and paper.
Planning, machining, assembly, measuring and testing keep their full time. s2 keeps 15 for tools not yet in the library; s6 keeps 20 for checking each sent value and writing those from plain gauges.
Gauge data are about parts, not used to rate machinists.
research_questions: Do first parts pass more often?

incremental.description: Machinist pairs gauges with the inspection record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library holds only half of the tools and half of the features are measured with plain gauges (6.7); high: library and digital gauges cover most work as designed (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss the look, sketch in CAD from standard parts, add dimensions, share the sketch and revise it.

steps.what: Machinist discusses the desired product appearance with the engineer or customer
Machinist prepares working sketches by hand
Machinist adds dimensions and notes to the sketch
Machinist checks the final sketch before sharing: dimensions match the intent, notes are clear and the right engineer is named
Machinist shares the checked sketch with the engineer: scanned and e-mailed today, shared from the CAD tool after the change
Machinist revises the sketch after feedback

tasks.design: Sketches are made in a simple CAD tool ({OTHER}) using a library of standard parts and the shop's common features, and the tool adds dimensions from the geometry for the machinist to check. The machinist checks each final sketch and shares it once from the same tool with the engineer. Discussing the look and revising stay with the machinist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sketches were drawn by hand, dimensioned by hand and scanned.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple CAD tools have part libraries, automatic dimensions and sharing.
tasks.still_hard: Some machinists sketch faster by hand for quick ideas.
tasks.human_edge: Showing what the part will look like in a way the customer understands.

evidence.claim: Simple CAD tools have part libraries, automatic dimensions and sharing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the product idea to the revised sketch; formal drawings are outside.
Input contract: standard parts library kept by the engineering department; fallback is drawing by hand.

Discussing, revising and the check before sharing keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because library parts replace drawing standard parts and the machinist still draws the rest; s3 keeps 50 because notes are still written and automatic dimensions are checked; s4 keeps 10 for the share itself.
Engineer time is outside the machinist's savings.

incremental.description: Machinist reports missing or wrong standard parts to engineering and keeps sketch versions in order.

approvals.approved_version: The dimensioned sketch exactly as checked by the machinist in s4b, shared once from the CAD tool with the named engineer; any change needs a new check and share.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many machinists keep sketching quick ideas by hand, so the library and automatic dimensions help little (15.6); high: sketches made in the CAD tool as designed (29.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The machinist keeps sorting, machining, measuring and judgement; sheets, catalogues and hand sketches shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A machinist whose records fill themselves while the machine runs.
